# `silk/compress/tar`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Read and write tar archives as streams, one block of bytes at a time.

## When to use
Use a [`TarReader`](#TarReader) to unpack a `.tar` file, or a `.tar.gz` file as a
`silk.compress.inflate.Decoder` decodes it. Give it the archive in pieces of any size with
[`TarReader.step`](#TarReader.impl.step): it reports each member's header, then the member's content, and it never
holds more than one header block. Use a [`TarWriter`](#TarWriter) to write an archive to the ambient
`silk.io.writer.Writer`: add members with [`TarWriter.file`](#TarWriter.impl.file) and [`TarWriter.directory`](#TarWriter.impl.directory), or
send a large file in pieces with [`TarWriter.beginFile`](#TarWriter.impl.beginFile) and [`TarWriter.writeContent`](#TarWriter.impl.writeContent), and
end the archive with [`TarWriter.finish`](#TarWriter.impl.finish). For a `.tar.gz`, provide a
`silk.compress.deflate.EncodeWriter` as the `Writer`. This module does not compress or
decompress.

## Details
The reader understands ustar, GNU, and pax archives: the ustar `prefix` field, GNU long names
and long link names, pax `path`, `linkpath`, and `size` records, and base-256 numbers. It does
not allocate and does not keep a borrow of your input. Each header's checksum is checked. A
member's path is checked before the member is reported: an absolute path, a backslash, a NUL,
or a `..` segment refuses the archive, so a caller that joins a path to a directory and creates
no links never writes outside it. Empty and `.` segments are allowed, because `tar -C dir .`
writes paths such as `./include/x.h`.

The writer writes ustar headers with fixed metadata: modification time 0, owner and group 0
with no names, and mode 644, or 755 for an executable file or a directory. A path longer than
100 bytes goes in the ustar `prefix` field when it splits at a `/`, else in a pax `path`
record. The same members in the same order give the same bytes on every host, so a checksum of
the archive names its content.

## Errors
- [`TarError`](#TarError) from [`TarReader.step`](#TarReader.impl.step) when a header is corrupt, the archive ends inside a
  member, a path is unsafe, or a long path does not fit the reader.
- [`TarError`](#TarError) from the writer when a path is one the reader would refuse, or when the members
  and their content come in the wrong order.
- `WriterError` from the writer when the ambient `Writer` fails.

## Examples
### Count the files of an archive given in small pieces
```silk
import silk.collections.slice {Slice}
import silk.compress.tar {TarError, TarKind, TarProgress, TarReader, TarStatus}
import silk.core.result {Result}

// Counts the regular files of `archive`, or answers -1 when it is not a valid tar archive. It
// gives the reader 100 bytes at a time, as a network or a decompressor would.
fn files(archive: &[u8]) -> i32 {
  let mut reader = TarReader.make()
  let mut count = 0
  let mut offset: usize = 0
  while true {
    let length = if archive.length - offset < 100 { archive.length - offset } else { 100 }
    let last = offset + length == archive.length
    let progress = match TarReader.step(&mut reader, Slice.view<u8>(archive, offset, length), last) {
      Result<TarProgress, TarError>.Success {value} => value
      Result<TarProgress, TarError>.Failure {..} => { return -1 }
    }
    offset = offset + progress.consumed
    if progress.status == TarStatus.Member && TarReader.member(&reader).kind == TarKind.File { count = count + 1 }
    if progress.status == TarStatus.End { return count }
  }
  return count
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let empty: [u8; 1024] = [0; 1024]
  return files(&empty)
}
```

### Write an archive and read it back
```silk
import silk.collections.slice {Slice}
import silk.compress.tar {TarError, TarProgress, TarReader, TarStatus, TarWriter}
import silk.core.effect {Effect}
import silk.core.result {Result}
import silk.io.writer {Writer, WriterError}

// A `Writer` that keeps up to 8 KiB in memory.
struct Memory {
  bytes: [u8; 8192],
  length: usize,
}

impl Writer for Memory {
  effect fn writeAll(self: &mut Self, value: &[u8]) -> () ! WriterError ? &mut Writer {
    if value.length > 8192 - self.length { fail Writer.failure() }
    Slice.copyInto<u8>(&mut self.bytes, self.length, value)
    self.length = self.length + value.length
  }

  effect fn flush(self: &mut Self) -> () ! WriterError ? &mut Writer { return () }
}

effect fn archive() -> () ! TarError | WriterError ? &mut Writer {
  let mut writer = TarWriter.make()
  run TarWriter.directory(&mut writer, b"app/bin")
  run TarWriter.file(&mut writer, b"app/bin/run", b"#!/bin/sh\n", true)
  // A file whose content arrives in pieces.
  run TarWriter.beginFile(&mut writer, b"app/README", 6, false)
  run TarWriter.writeContent(&mut writer, b"hel")
  run TarWriter.writeContent(&mut writer, b"lo\n")
  return run TarWriter.finish(move writer)
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32 ! TarError | WriterError {
  let mut memory = Memory {bytes: [0; 8192], length: 0}
  run archive() |> Effect.provideMut<Writer>(&mut memory)
  let mut reader = TarReader.make()
  let mut offset: usize = 0
  let mut members = 0
  while true {
    let input = Slice.view<u8>(&memory.bytes, offset, memory.length - offset)
    let progress = match TarReader.step(&mut reader, input, true) {
      Result<TarProgress, TarError>.Success {value} => value
      Result<TarProgress, TarError>.Failure {..} => { return 1 }
    }
    offset = offset + progress.consumed
    if progress.status == TarStatus.Member { members = members + 1 }
    if progress.status == TarStatus.End { break }
  }
  return if members == 3 { 0 } else { 2 }
}
```

## `TarMember`

```silk
pub struct TarMember<'a>
```

The header of one member of a tar archive: its checked path, its kind, and its size.

### Details
The member's path is `prefix/name`, `name` alone when `prefix` is empty, or `prefix` alone when
`name` is empty, as ustar writes a long directory path. A GNU long name or a pax `path` record
comes back as `name` with an empty `prefix`. The slices borrow the [`TarReader`](#TarReader), so copy what
you keep before the next [`TarReader.step`](#TarReader.impl.step).

<a id="TarReader"></a>

## `TarReader`

```silk
pub struct TarReader
```

A tar reader that takes the archive in pieces of any size.

### When to use
Make one with [`TarReader.make`](#TarReader.impl.make) and call [`TarReader.step`](#TarReader.impl.step) with the archive's bytes until it
returns `End`. Each call consumes a prefix of its input, and the next call takes the input
after that prefix. The archive can come from memory, a file, a socket, or a
`silk.compress.inflate.Decoder`.

### Details
The reader does not allocate and does not borrow your input. It holds one 512-byte header and
room for a long path and a long link target, [`PATH_LIMIT`](#PATH_LIMIT) bytes each. Content is not copied:
a `Content` progress names a prefix of the input that you gave. When you give the whole
archive at once, each file's content comes back in one piece. The reader stops at the first
all-zero block. After a failure, each step fails with `InvalidUse`.

<a id="TarReader.impl.step"></a>

### Method `step`

```silk
pub fn step(self: &mut Self, input: &[u8], last: bool) -> Result<TarProgress, TarError>
```

Reads from the start of `input` and returns how much it consumed and what it found.

#### Details
On the next call, give only the input after the consumed prefix, followed by any new bytes.
The call returns at the first member header (`Member`), with the content of the current file
(`Content`, always from the start of `input`), at the end of the archive (`End`), or when it
consumed all of `input` (`NeedInput`). Set `last` when `input` holds the rest of the archive:
then the archive may end without its end-of-archive blocks, at a member boundary or after a
file's content without its final padding. GNU long-name and pax headers are read as part of
the member they name, and pax global headers are skipped.

#### Errors
- [`TarError`](#TarError) with `Truncated` when `last` is set and the archive ends inside a header or a
  member, `BadHeader` when a checksum, number, or pax record is invalid, `UnsafePath` when
  the member's path is absolute, holds a backslash or a NUL, or has a `..` segment, and
  `PathTooLong` for a long path over [`PATH_LIMIT`](#PATH_LIMIT) bytes. After a failure, each step fails
  with `InvalidUse`.

<a id="TarReader.impl.member"></a>

### Method `member`

```silk
pub fn member<'a>(self: &'a Self) -> TarMember<'a>
```

Returns the header of the member that the last step reported with `Member`.

#### Details
The member borrows the reader. It is valid until the next [`TarReader.step`](#TarReader.impl.step), which may
overwrite the bytes it names. Before the first `Member`, it returns an empty member of kind
`Other`.

<a id="TarReader.impl.remaining"></a>


<a id="TarWriter"></a>

## `TarWriter`

```silk
pub struct TarWriter
```

A tar archive being written to the ambient `Writer`, one member at a time.

### When to use
Make one with [`TarWriter.make`](#TarWriter.impl.make), add members in the order the archive should list them, and
end the archive with [`TarWriter.finish`](#TarWriter.impl.finish). Use [`TarWriter.file`](#TarWriter.impl.file) for a file whose content is
in memory, and [`TarWriter.beginFile`](#TarWriter.impl.beginFile) then [`TarWriter.writeContent`](#TarWriter.impl.writeContent) for a file whose content
comes in pieces.

### Details
The writer holds no buffer: each header, each piece of content, and each block's padding goes
to the `Writer` as it comes. It writes ustar headers with fixed metadata: modification time
zero, owner and group zero with empty names, and mode 644 for a file, 755 for an executable
file or a directory. The same members in the same order therefore always give the same bytes,
on any host. A path longer than the 100-byte name field is split into the ustar prefix and name
at a `/` when it fits, and is otherwise written in a pax `path` record. A file of 8 GiB or more
records its size in base-256. [`TarReader`](#TarReader) reads every archive the writer makes.

### Gotchas
The writer does not flush the `Writer`. Flush or finish the provider after
[`TarWriter.finish`](#TarWriter.impl.finish).

### Method `file`

```silk
pub effect fn file(self: &mut Self, path: &[u8], content: &[u8], executable: bool) -> ()
    ! TarError | WriterError
    ? &mut Writer
```

Adds the regular file `path` holding `content`, with mode 755 when `executable` and 644
otherwise.

#### Errors
- [`TarError`](#TarError) with `UnsafePath` when `path` is empty, absolute, ends in `/`, or holds a
  backslash, a NUL, or a `..` segment, and `InvalidUse` when the last file begun with
  [`TarWriter.beginFile`](#TarWriter.impl.beginFile) did not get all its content. Nothing is written.
- `WriterError` when the `Writer` fails.


Writes the header of the regular file `path` of `size` bytes, with mode 755 when
`executable` and 644 otherwise. Send its content with [`TarWriter.writeContent`](#TarWriter.impl.writeContent).

#### Errors
- [`TarError`](#TarError) with `UnsafePath` when `path` is empty, absolute, ends in `/`, or holds a
  backslash, a NUL, or a `..` segment, and `InvalidUse` when the last file did not get all
  its content. Nothing is written.
- `WriterError` when the `Writer` fails.
